page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is a compute-focused instance within Azure's ARM-based general purpose lineup, engineered for workloads requiring high thread counts with moderate memory density. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server is driven by 32 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores running at 3.4 GHz with one thread per physical core. Cache hierarchy includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 128 MB L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via hardware AES instructions. The configuration provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is provisioned without local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring external block storage for persistent operational data.

Benchmark assessments highlight strong parallel execution and exceptional memory subsystem throughput. In synthetic memory benchmarks, large-block uncached read bandwidth reaches 449.06 GB/sec and write bandwidth achieves 188.51 GB/sec, placing the platform in the top tier of evaluated hardware. PassMark database operations and overall memory testing also rate in the top tier. Multithreaded execution is robust, evidenced by strong results in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang software compilation. Application-level performance remains competitive, with Redis SET operations sustaining 61.87 million operations per second and static web serving reaching 50.4 GB/sec. Conversely, single-thread performance across stress-ng and Geekbench remains average, and LLM prompt processing for large 70B parameter models falls in the lower tiers.

The architectural profile yields high resource efficiency for horizontally scaling CPU-bound applications. Dedicating an entire physical core to each vCPU avoids hyperthreading contention, ensuring predictable latency for multi-threaded processes. However, the reduced memory footprint of 2.0 GB per vCPU poses a tradeoff for large in-memory databases, and the absence of attached local storage means disk I/O depends entirely on network-attached storage performance. The server is suited for software build systems, CI/CD runners, multi-threaded compression pipelines, Redis key-value stores, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is a general-purpose, compute-dense virtual machine based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon clocked at 3.4 GHz, it provides 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, backed by 128 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes 64.0 GB of memory, establishing a 2 GB per core ratio, but includes no local storage or onboard GPUs, relying entirely on remote storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D32pls_v6 displays top-tier memory bandwidth exceeding 449 GB/sec on uncached reads and outstanding database processing capability. It delivers strong multi-core performance across stress-ng, Clang compilation, and static web serving, while single-core compute and large-model inference remain moderate. Offering a resource-efficient balance of core density and high memory throughput, this server is well configured for multi-threaded compilation pipelines, Redis caching, static web hosting, and containerized microservices.
